posts.body:
Hi all,
I am making some changes to the way the UI works in my game (more a prototype than a game, but never mind) and I was looking for a way to call up the Formation Menu, which as far as I understand cannot be called like the other menus by pushing using the SceneManager a corresponding Scene object. I looked for a solution in this forum and in a couple threads I saw people saying that it was possible to cal the Formation Menu using script commands but I could not find any concrete code example that I could use or at least adapt.
Right now I have implemented formation changes by using a combination of text boxes, input numbers and direct calls to the $gameParty methods, but it looks ugly and not very intuitive.
Does anyone know what kind of functions calls would be necessary to call up the standard Formation Menu programmatically (i.e. from a .js file or within an event)? Thanks in advance for the suggestions!

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
I don't believe you can, without rewriting some of how the menu itself works.
By default, Formation is a mode of the menu scene. So you can use script calls to get into it:
Code:
SceneManager.push(Scene_Menu);
SceneManager._scene.commandFormation();
but the second line won't function until the scene itself is loaded, which is not instantaneous. So simply entering those as two lines of code like that won't work. You have to push the scene change, then once it's been constructed you can do commandFormation() instead of scrolling to and selecting the formation command.
Or you rewrite the menu so that's the default mode and change the default command bindings.
Or you make a second scene that's a copy of Scene_Menu but has that different default mode and command bindings, and push to that scene.
Or you event it.
Or you use something like Yanfly's Party Manager which gives you an interface for this outside of the formation mode of the menu.

I would interpret the second option as creating a Scene object that is a subclass of Scene_Menu and overriding whatever method is called when the scene is pushed with "SceneManager._scene.commandFormation()" but I am not sure how to go about it in JavaScript (I also apologise if my terminology sounds weird, I am new to RPG Maker and when it comes to scripting I am essentially winging it based on my past experience with Java).
As to "eventing it", I am drawing a blank - I have not seen any event command that I can use to call up menus, just to enable/disable access to them.
Once again thanks in advance for any help I can get!

I'm not sure what you mean - can you provide a screenshot? There is no sub-window - all that the Formation command does is move the cursor from the left side of the screen, where you have the menu commands, over to the right side of the screen, where you have the actors' faces.
All of the menu windows are open all of the time in this process, nothing visually changes.

Thanks for the clarification. I guess I do want a custom Scene, one that replicates the functionality of the main menu as far as the party composition is concerned. In other words, I'd like to have a Scene_Formation that I can push with the SceneManager to make the list of actors' faces
alone
(i.e. with no list "Item, Skill, etc." alongside it) appear and and allow the player to change the order of the actors if they so wish. I thought I could copy or adapt existing code since the functionality exists already, but I could not find any resource explaining clearly how the internals of the Scenes work.
I will give a little background: I felt that the basic interaction mode in RPG Maker was a bit limited, so I programmed a couple of new actions, such as "Examine" or "Use Item" that can be used within the game map (basically, they allow the implemetation of puzzles like the ones found in graphical adventures). I bound these additional actions to keyboard shortcuts, but I wanted them in the game menu as well. As I said, it's not clear to me how Scenes work, so I "evented" a new main menu using exactly the tutorial in link you are mentioning (I did a bit more actually, my custom menu has also mouse support, the menu in the tutorial is exclusively keyboard-driven). In the end, I was able to implement my new commands and to replicate all the commands in the standard main menu in my custom-made menu except for "Formation", because it does not have its dedicated Scene object nor an event command.
Right now I have implemented the "Formation"
functionality
, but it's quite ugly to see and it would be nice to have the same look and feel of the others. Rather than writing something from scratch I thought to ask around to see if someone had an already-made solution or could at least point me in the right direction to program one myself. From Eliaquim's reply and yours I suspect I have no such luck, but I hope at least now it's clear what I'm after!
